entities.summary:
Conrad of Ascoli was an Italian Friar Minor and missionary who played a pivotal role in the spread of Christianity during the Middle Ages. Born into a noble family in Ascoli, Italy around 1230, Conrad dedicated his life to serving God and the Church. He traveled extensively throughout Europe, establishing monasteries and schools, and preaching the Gospel to various populations. Conrad's influence extended beyond his own region, as he worked closely with other prominent clergy and nobles to promote religious understanding and cooperation.

Conrad of Ascoli is also notable for his association with the Franciscan Order, a movement that emphasized poverty, simplicity, and devotion to God. His commitment to these values resonated deeply with the people he encountered, earning him a reputation as a compassionate and effective missionary. Conrad's legacy can be seen in the many institutions and communities he helped establish, which continued to thrive long after his passing.

Conrad of Ascoli's feast day is celebrated on April 19, marking the anniversary of his death in 1289. This event has been commemorated by numerous religious orders and historical societies, ensuring that Conrad's memory remains an important part of Christian tradition.
